name: Meni
title: Pagan Fortune God
summary: Meni is the name of a pagan deity mentioned in Isaiah 65:11, who was worshipped by apostate Israelites. The name likely means 'fortune' or 'destiny' and refers to a Mesopotamian god of fate. The prophet Isaiah condemns those who abandon the Lord to worship Meni and other false gods.

keyEvents.title: Condemnation of Idolatry
keyEvents.description: Isaiah condemns the Israelites who forsake the Lord, setting a table for the idol god Gad (Fortune) and filling the cup for Meni (Destiny). This represents a serious apostasy from Israel's covenant with God.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on the Apostates
keyEvents.description: In the context of Isaiah 65, God warns of judgment against those who worship foreign gods like Meni and promises punishment for their rebellion and disobedience to the true God.

keyEvents.title: The Contrast Between God's Servants and Idolaters
keyEvents.description: Isaiah draws a sharp contrast between those who faithfully serve the Lord and those who have turned to idolatry, such as the worship of Meni. God's servants will be blessed, while idolaters face judgment.

keyEvents.title: God's Call to Repentance from Idolatry
keyEvents.description: Throughout the book of Isaiah, Israel is called to turn away from foreign gods and return to the one true God, providing context for the condemnation of the worship of Meni.
